entries.title: Everything You Need to Know for Commanders-Seahawks
entries.summary: Key matchups, how to watch, pregame reading and more.
entries.content:
The Commanders go into Sunday’s home opener with an 0-2 record and starting quarterback Jayden Daniels sidelined with an elbow injury. The reigning champion Seahawks come to town 2-0, and could see their starting quarterback return from an injury of his own.

Here’s everything you need to know.

Kickoff: 1 p.m. at Northwest Stadium, Summerfield, Md.

TV: Fox

Betting Lines

Lines from DraftKings, as of Saturday. 

Spread: Commanders +7.5
Money line: Commanders +310, Seahawks -395
Over/under: 40.5 points

Pregame Reading

After Daniels dislocated the same elbow for the second time in 10 months, The Washington Sun’s Dave Sheinin wrote that the Commanders need to start asking themselves if the team can count on him long-term.

GM Adam Peters said Friday that the team does not expect Daniels to have surgery or need to go on injured reserve, after the quarterback sought additional opinions on the injury this week. There is no immediate timetable for his return, with the team considering him week-to-week.

While Daniels is out, veteran backup Marcus Mariota will step in, with a focus on playing within the offense and not trying to be the hero all by himself.

About the Seahawks

Starting quarterback Sam Darnold is “on a good track” to return Sunday, according to coach Mike Macdonald, after Darnold suffered a glute injury in the season-opener against the Patriots. Backup Drew Lock has led the Seahawks to a 2-0 start in Darnold’s absence and has kept the offense humming. In Sunday’s win against the Cardinals, Lock connected with star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba for three touchdowns.

Macdonald also apologized to Broncos coach Sean Payton for describing the “cold war” that took place between the two teams in 2024, when the Seahawks watched videos of the Broncos’ training camp, which Payton thought was a violation of NFL rules. Macdonald said that his comments, which were part of an interview, weren’t meant to be public.

“I’m responsible for what I say, really no matter the circumstance, whether you’re mic’d up, whether you’re not, whether you have some type of understanding,” Macdonald said. “So I fell short in that moment. So it stings for me, frankly, but it’s something I’m definitely gonna learn from.”

One Big Question

What can the Commanders get out of Mariota?

Mariota was 11-for-16 on Sunday with 111 yards passing and a touchdown after coming in for Daniels. But there is a big difference between the suspect Cowboys defense he faced then and the one he’ll see Sunday; Seattle again has one of the best defenses in the league, a year after the unit helped carry the team to a Super Bowl victory.

If Mariota can lead the Commanders to an upset win or keep the team competitive in a loss, it would bring some optimism that they can still make something of this season.

Quote of the Week

“At the end of the day, it’s my job,” Mariota told reporters Sunday after stepping in for Daniels. “I just never want it to be in these types of circumstances. With as much experience that I’ve had, I feel comfortable. … I really like what [offensive coordinator] coach Blough’s doing. I believe in this system, and we’ll get this thing working.”

entries.title: DHS Denies Agents Were Told to Stand Down Arrests for Non-Criminals
entries.summary: The Daily Wire reported ICE agents had been told to stop arresting those without a criminal record.
entries.content:
The Department of Homeland Security denied reports that immigration agents had been told over the weekend to stop arresting non-criminals during their enforcement efforts.

“This is false. No one is off the table. We will continue to arrest any and all illegal aliens that come into our path,” DHS wrote in an email and shared to X, adding that “ICE has initiated a nationwide public safety surge in sanctuary cities where our brave officers will be targeting criminal illegal aliens.”

The Daily Wire first reported that a new policy was aimed at only targeting immigrants with a criminal record and would also end “collateral arrests,” which occur when individuals that are not the focus of immigration enforcement officials are arrested in an operation.

Fox News reporter Bill Melugin said on X that he spoke with President Donald Trump as well as several ICE and DHS sources about the guidance and was “told it’s erroneous, was some type of ‘miscommunication’ during conversations about prioritizing ‘worst first.’”

New guidance went out to ICE field offices on Saturday night reaffirming that there has been no change in immigration enforcement policy, Melugin wrote in a post Saturday, and the “collateral arrests” of those without a criminal history will continue.

DHS did not immediately respond to a request from The Washington Sun to confirm that the department sent out guidance reaffirming ICE’s policies.

The Trump administration’s federal immigration enforcement efforts have drawn scrutiny from Democrats and members of local communities where ICE is present.

Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan man with no known criminal record, was shot by an ICE officer on Sept. 20 in Austin. Garces Perez had a final order of removal, according to DHS, but his lawyer argued that he had missed an immigration hearing because a notice was sent to an old address.

Since the Trump administration crackdown began, 21 people have been shot by ICE agents, resulting in eight fatalities, according to an ABC News’ report last week.

The Trump administration has engaged in an aggressive approach to immigration enforcement efforts, with more than 605,000 deportations and another 1.9 million people self-deporting — meaning the individual leaves the U.S. rather than being removed by the government — according to the White House’s website.
entries.author: Jenna Monnin

entries.title: 130,000 Out of Power as Nor’easter Floods the Northeast
entries.summary: High tides are threatening coastal areas and strong winds are slamming into communities from New Jersey to New England.
entries.content:
By Leah Willingham

BOSTON — A powerful nor’easter battered the Northeast again on Sunday, flooding coastal communities and leaving tens of thousands of homes and businesses without power as forecasters warned that another round of high tides could inundate vulnerable shorelines.

The slow-moving storm, which killed a New York City housing authority worker when a tree fell Saturday, was expected to linger through Sunday with heavy rain, strong winds and dangerous surf from New Jersey to New England.

The storm remained just south of Long Island and east of northern New Jersey on Sunday morning and was expected to loop around the area for roughly another 24 hours, said Bob Oravec, a lead forecaster with the National Weather Service in College Park, Maryland.

The worst of the remaining rainfall was expected Sunday from northern New Jersey through New York City and Long Island into southern New England. The storm was gradually weakening, Oravec said, but the threat of tidal flooding would linger through high-tide cycles Sunday morning and again in the evening.

“The most impactful parts of the storm are likely going to be the high winds and the tidal flooding,” Oravec said.

The nor’easter triggered memories of Superstorm Sandy, which left behind over $60 billion in damage across the eastern U.S. in 2012. While this storm’s impact has been nowhere near that, it could be the first of several along the East Coast this fall because of an El Niño climate pattern that’s disrupting this year’s weather.

More than 130,000 customers were without power across the Northeast and mid-Atlantic Sunday morning, according to PowerOutage.us.

The most widespread outages were along the New Jersey shore, New York's Long Island and coastal counties in Connecticut. Toppled trees across Long Island damaged homes and cars, blocked streets and downed numerous utility lines.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency said response coordination centers in impacted regions were operating at an “enhanced posture,” and teams were on standby in New England in case of widespread outages.

On Saturday in New Jersey and New York, some people kayaked down flooded streets. Others headed to beaches to try to surf the higher-than-usual waves. Emergency crews in Sea Bright, New Jersey, rescued a woman and her dog after their vehicle became trapped in floodwaters, ABC7 reported.

In Surf City, New Jersey, water rose inside a marina where workers had moved equipment to higher ground, and owner Kenny Formica said customers reported boats and Jet Skis missing or blown from their lifts. In Norfolk, Virginia, floodwaters left passing cars pushing wakes through some streets.

The storm also disrupted travel throughout the region. Hundreds of flights were canceled at Boston Logan International Airport, while flooding cut off highway access to North Carolina’s Hatteras Island, stranding visitors and forcing one couple to scramble to relocate their wedding after most of their roughly 45 guests were unable to reach the island.

___

AP journalist Julie Walker contributed from New York.
entries.author: The Associated Press

entries.title: Five Men Arrested on Suspected Terrorism Near a U.K. Air Base Used by the U.S.
entries.summary: RAF Fairford has been used by American forces for limited strikes in the Iran war.
entries.content:
By Pan Pylas

LONDON — UK police said Sunday that five men arrested in the middle of the night near an air base used by the United States during its war against Iran are being held on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.

London’s Metropolitan Police, which takes the lead on potential terrorism activities, said in a statement that police received a call at 12:45 a.m. related to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be traveling toward the air base.

The five men were initially arrested on suspicion of committing offenses under the Explosives Act in the Whelford area, which backs onto RAF Fairford, the base that hosts the headquarters of the U.S. Air Force’s 501st Combat Support Wing and the 420th Air Base Squadron. The base is U.K. owned and U.S. operated under an agreement dating back to the Cold War.

Fairford has been used by American forces for strictly limited strikes during the war with Iran. After the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran on Feb. 28, the U.K. government allowed the American military to use the Fairford base to strike Iranian missile sites. Iran has said bombers flying from the base have been used for strikes beyond the original remit.

President Donald Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One that U.S. officials are working with British police.

"It was an amazing job," Trump said of the police. "We had them under investigation. They they were looking to do big damage to our ports."

Police gave no details as to the nationality of those arrested.

“We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody,” said Vicki Evans, the Met's deputy assistant commissioner. “As you would expect, we are working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident.”

She said a 400-meter cordon has been put in place around the three vehicles that raised suspicion while the army conducts examinations. As a precaution, around 85 households have been evacuated whilst these examinations take place.

Aerial footage from Sky News appeared to show a bomb disposal robot roaming between three white trucks. The rear doors of two of the vans were open and large black items could be seen scattered around. The robot appeared to be working toward getting access to the third truck.

The local Gloucestershire police force said the situation appeared to be “contained.”

A spokesperson for the U.S. Air Force said U.S. and British personnel “remain vigilant” and will take appropriate actions to ensure safety of all those at the base.

“For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures," the spokesperson said. “We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families."

The arrests come at a time of heightened tensions around the threat from hostile states to the U.K., with Russia and Iran among those that have used proxies to commit crimes on their behalf on British soil. In March, officials said the number of national security cases involving activity by hostile states including Iran increased 50% in the six months to December 2025.

Residents in a number of properties in Whelford have been taken to a nearby recreation center.

Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, said a resident had reported three “suspicious vans” in the village in the early hours of Sunday morning.

“There were several police, three police cars in the drive, and they said you need to evacuate, there’s been a major incident, said he couldn’t elaborate,” he said.

Britain's Defense Secretary Wes Streeting thanked the emergency and specialist teams who responded to the incident.

“We can be reassured that this is being dealt with," he said.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is receiving updates on the situation, his office said.
entries.author: The Associated Press

entries.title: The AI Bros Are Partying
entries.summary: Hundreds gathered at a bitcoin-themed bar in D.C. to counterprogram the national backlash against data centers and AI.
entries.content:
The Loudoun County Iced Tea, an homage to Virginia’s “data center alley,” was peach-forward and watery, with a flat finish. The “SMR-tini,” a play on the abbreviation for small nuclear reactors, was a very good espresso martini, The Washington Sun can confirm. And the “Closed Loop Spritz” — made with prosecco, elderflower and soda — sold out before these reporters could conduct any research.

One bartender declined a tip and offered assurance they were more than well compensated for the event.

On Saturday, PubKey, the cryptocurrency-themed bar in downtown D.C., hosted hundreds — a thousand RSVP’d to the Partiful invite — for a celebration of data centers.

It was a party planned on the defensive, counterprogramming what the invite described as a “bipartisan psychosis” over data centers. Three men who work in libertarian and conservative spaces organized it: Jonas Du, a writer for Pirate Wires, a media company founded by conservative commentator and Peter Thiel protegé Mike Solana; Ed Tarnowski, a resident fellow at the R Street Institute; and Casey Given, the CEO of Young Voices, which supports “thought leaders for liberty in the digital age.”

At a time when fears around AI are mounting — polls show three-quarters of Americans oppose local data centers and people across the country are organizing to stop them from being built — hundreds were lining up in the rain hoping to get into a party where people were clinking glasses to the very infrastructure that communities are fighting tooth and nail.
Data Center Party Decor (6240x4160, AR: 1.50)Comeandtakeit lead.JPG (6240x4160, AR: 1.50)Partygoers included engineers, the executives of small AI-driven companies and nonprofits, the owner of a bitcoin mining operation, federal workers, trade group representatives, the parliamentarian of Rhode Island’s Republican Party and more than a few people who had heard about the party online and were drawn there out of pure curiosity. And journalists — lots of journalists.

“I feel the least autistic I’ve ever felt in this setting,” a teacher named Olivia said, looking around. She tagged along with a friend, she said.

The party planners said the idea was to gather all the right minds in one place to engineer a way past the greatest friction facing data center development: politics.

“So much of this conversation felt constrained to very specific corners of Twitter,” Du said. “At the end of the day, if you want to make policy progress, you have to put the right people to advance the goals in one room together — and what better way to do it than a grand old party?”

But for the most part, the event seemed more geared toward mocking the data center backlash than addressing it on its merits.

There was a strong vein of snark. A DJ cycled through high-energy pop music behind a “come and take it” poster. Signage included a “Visit Loudon County, VA” display, and a “Virginia is for Servers” poster, designed to resemble the state’s trademarked “Virginia is for Lovers” tourism tag line. A white paper from the Open Source AI Foundation describing a pro-data center national ballot initiative program was splayed out next to the downstairs bar.

In many ways it was quintessentially D.C. — a nerd prom after hours that was equal parts politically heightened and distinctly removed from politics.

“The party is like a D.C. party. You talk to people from, like, think tanks,” said Noah Swank, who works at a think tank.

Many attendees wore suits, and some wore them with sneakers. Other outfits included knit sweaters with American flags and the word “reindustrialize,” bitcoin pins, and one person with a hat that resembled a Lite-Brite.

Another indication of a “D.C. party”? The ratio of men to women.

“Like, four or five to one,” Swank said. “Not ideal.”

In a whiskey lounge adjacent to the dance floor, sponsored by the Bitcoin Policy Institute, a quiet chess game unfolded in one corner, while men drunkenly explained policy ideas to one another, raising their voices over the thump of heavy bass. In the basement there was a VIP room with a three-part jazz band.

At the party were some of the nation’s leading tech voices — among them policy wonks entrusted with proposing potential guardrails for the quickly developing technology that is AI. 

There were industry speakers, who focused on beating China, conquering “fear of the unknown,” and the potential for AI to transform the world for the better. “Freedom” and “liberty” were frequent refrains. Jasmine Sun, a contributor to The Atlantic, also made a toast in support of building more data centers, chalking the backlash up to misinformation.

“It was really interesting to see how many people — proud Americans, farmers, union workers — didn’t understand what was being done,” she said, describing a road trip she took to chronicle the data center backlash (a project that landed her interviews with Nate Silver and Ezra Klein). “I just thought ‘We have so much more work to do to help people understand.’”

But it was unclear if the crowd was interested in facing its detractors.

Every few minutes, a protester in cocktail attire hopped onto the stage, raising objections about environmental impacts and the dangers of AI development. They were drowned out by the crowd’s chants of “USA, USA.”

One attendee near the front called a protester a “bitch” and told her to “go on a diet.” One by one, the protesters were escorted off the stage by other attendees, and, eventually, security guards.

“You know who doesn’t believe in freedom, is the freaks who were just up here charging the stage,” Adam Thierer with the R Street Institute shouted into the microphone after one such interruption. “Let’s show people what this fight is all about about data centers. It’s a fight about the freedom of the future of America to develop.”

Another person in attendance, who requested anonymity because of their work for an AI safety nonprofit, described the backlash as “slopulist bullshit.”

“There are real issues of like, cybersecurity and distillation, and bad actors using AI for bioterrorism, or regular terrorism, for that matter, and those are all real, right? Those are real threats,” they said. “But the idea that if we stop data centers, and that’s going to change, is ridiculous. It doesn’t make sense.”

Data Center Party VA Servers (6240x4160, AR: 1.50)Protester Data Center Party (6240x4160, AR: 1.50)It’s unclear whether an industry-sponsored echo chamber like “Data After Dark” can move the needle backward at this point. Many Democrats are riding the anti-data center wave, and Republicans are distancing themselves from the issue, while President Donald Trump maintains a staunch pro-data center stance. Trump has used the power of the executive branch to pave a smoother path for their development. But their overwhelming unpopularity continues to scramble political ties ahead of the midterms.

Grace and Livi Plihal, who came to the event intent on heckling partiers, said a lack of information wasn’t the problem.

“We’ve been really kind of in despair over seeing how [AI is] maybe going to put us out of our jobs,” said Grace. Her sister Livi, an artist, is looking to find work but discouraged by the use of generative AI to create art for businesses that may otherwise have hired a human.

Grace, a therapist, said she worried her clients were talking to ChatGPT in between sessions and getting “horrible, unfactual answers.”

The Plihals said they also worried about noise and environmental damage from AI infrastructure and the potential for higher power bills, two concerns central to the local backlash against projects.

Those worries were familiar territory for some attendees.

“I’m a pro-AI advocate, one of the biggest names in town. My mom hates data centers. I love her. Bless her heart,” Nathan Leamer, executive director of the advocacy organization Build American AI, said.

Leamer compared data centers to highways: a development that could fundamentally reshape the country, in his eyes, for the better. (His mom, he said, doesn’t care about the highway near her home – despite the noise.)

Channing Pear, who founded Anvil Labs, which helps manufacturers and industrial companies roll out AI systems, offered a different comparison.

“Until everybody has an Iron Man suit, and can 3D print their food from a microwave by pressing a button, and teleport and go to space, then we haven’t solved enough problems,” Pear said. “Just imagine how much technology we need to build in order to get to that point.”
entries.author: Mara Hoplamazian, Emily Kennard

entries.title: Commanders Stun the Seahawks For a 33-31 Win
entries.summary: Washington pulls off a big upset in its home opener, knocking off the defending Super Bowl champs to avoid an 0-3 start.
entries.content:
An interception return for a touchdown from a fill-in linebacker and a clutch performance from a backup quarterback lifted the Commanders to an improbable and much-needed win Sunday, as Washington knocked off the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks 33-31 in its home opener.

The victory improves the Commanders' record to 1-2 and allows them to avoid a dreaded 0-3 start — providing hope for the team's longer-term prospects as it awaits the return of injured starting quarterback Jayden Daniels.

Linebacker Kain Medrano, filling in for Leo Chenal, who left the game with a neck injury, picked off Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold with just under four minutes left in the fourth quarter and returned it for a score, helping set the Commanders up for the win.

Quarterback Marcus Mariota, filling in for Daniels, threw for 183 yards and three touchdowns and sealed the victory with a 9-yard scramble on third and 7 on the team’s final drive. And Terry McLaurin, off to one of the slowest starts of career, finished with 77 yards on six catches, including his first touchdown of the season.

But it was Medrano, a sixth-round pick from a season ago who had played zero defensive snaps before Sunday, and his defensive teammates who might have had the biggest impact on the outcome. The Commanders' defense, which entered the game with zero turnovers through two weeks, forced three on the day — a recovered fumble by defensive tackle Tim Settle and an interception off a tipped pass by rookie linebacker Sonny Styles joining Medrano's pick in helping lead Washington to the win.
entries.author: Martenzie Johnson

entries.title: MLB Pitched the Trump Administration About a Game in a National Park
entries.summary: The White House said the push for the game is “not a Presidential directive.”
entries.content:
Major League Baseball approached the Trump administration about hosting a stand-alone game in a national park, MLB and White House officials confirmed on Sunday.

A National Park Service official visited Grand Teton National Park last week to scout potential locations for the baseball park, according to The Washington Post, which first reported on the outreach.

“The MLB came to the Administration asking if it was possible to host a game at a national park, similar to the Field of Dreams game,” a White House official said in a statement. “This is not a Presidential directive, nor is it being directed by the White House. It’s also not being driven by the Department of Interior.”

MLB proposed hosting a game at a national park following the success of other special event matches, an MLB official told The Washington Sun on the condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to speak publicly. The league has hosted several games at non-traditional venues — including games in Iowa paying homage to the 1989 “Field of Dreams” movie, a game at a motor speedway and one at an active military fort.

MLB is also exploring other ideas in addition to a potential game at a national park.

The White House official added that it is the MLB’s “prerogative” to visit any potential game locations at national parks — though “no decisions have been made by the MLB and no permits have been granted by NPS.”

Frank Lands, a deputy director for the National Park Service, visited Grand Teton National Park last week and looked at three potential locations for a baseball park, according to the Post.

Luther Propst, a Teton County commissioner, told The Sun that he spotted Lands on Thursday at the Murie Spirit of Conservation Awards at Murie Ranch, which is located inside the Grand Teton park boundaries.

Propst and another member of the county commission said they did not receive any notice regarding the MLB’s proposal or administration officials scouting locations for the game at the park.

“He didn't bring up why he was there,” Propst said. “Obviously, I didn't know anything about it.”

Propst is planning to suggest Monday during the commission’s regularly scheduled weekly meeting that it write a letter to MLB encouraging them to visit their county to “get a sense of why this is a bad idea.” A majority of the commission will have to agree for them to write to the MLB, the White House, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum or the Wyoming congressional delegation, Propst said.

“The response from our constituents has been, ‘Are you kidding me?’” Propst added.

The commissioner also noted that the lack of communication from the Interior Department, which oversees the National Park Service, is notable because Burgum in June 2025 approved Secretarial Order 3434, which directs the department to strengthen its outreach with “gateway communities” — areas adjacent to or that serve as access points to national parks.

“You would think an administration that pushed that idea of S.O. 3434 would make a special effort to communicate with neighboring counties, but in this case, they did not,” Propst said.

The Interior Department and the National Park Service did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

President Donald Trump has embraced hosting sporting events on federal lands in the past year, with several of the events coinciding with the nation’s 250th anniversary. Trump hosted a UFC event on the White House lawn in June and an IndyCar race around the National Mall in August.

National parks do not expressly prohibit hosting sporting events, but official NPS policy for “appropriate use” of the federal lands “emphasize[s] appropriate recreation consistent with the protection of the park.”

Since the start of Trump’s second term, the Interior Department has undergone major staffing shakeups and proposed new ways to organize the NPS that would centralize authority among the larger parks.

The Sun reported in August that Trump administration officials pushed for NPS staff to find a way to enable a land exchange between Yosemite National Park and a private developer to build a road connecting property outside of the park to one of Yosemite’s main thoroughfares.

The proposal generated significant public outcry, with more than 150 lawmakers urging the Interior Department to abandon the land proposal.
entries.author: Jenna Monnin

entries.title: A 2024 Trump Campaign Ad Is the Latest Taxpayer-Funded Messaging
entries.summary: The 30-second spot is virtually identical to one Trump's 2024 campaign aired.
entries.content:
The Trump administration is using taxpayer funds to air a television advertisement from Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign in the latest in a series of ads promoting the president ahead of the midterms that the White House maintains are “public service announcements.”

The 30-second video, which is virtually identical to one that aired in 2024, shows Trump walking down a hallway as his voice can be heard warning of a “final battle” against “globalists” and “warmongers.” The black-and-white video ends with Trump staring straight into the camera lens with a message that says: “Paid for by the U.S. Government.” The 2024 iteration of the ad from the Trump campaign urged viewers to “Join President Trump’s Fight for America.”

Lawmakers of both parties have criticized the new series of ads for their inherently political nature and the use of taxpayer dollars. The White House maintains they are like the ones used by past presidents, though those previous ads promoted particular policies, not Oval Office occupants.

Spending on the latest ad already topped about $319,000, according to AdImpact, which tracks media spending.

“With you at my side, we will demolish the ‘deep state.’ We will expel the war mongers from our government. We will drive out the globalists; we will cast out the communists, Marxists, and fascists,” he says in the narration. “We will throw off the sick political class that hates our country. We will rout the fake news media, and we will liberate America from these villains once and for all.”

It’s in addition to a minute-long ad that began airing Friday and features scenic videos of Mount Rushmore at night with quotes and clips from Trump’s Fourth of July weekend speech there honoring the country’s 250th anniversary. An earlier 30-second spot that began airing on Wednesday features clips of Trump talking about defeating communism interspersed with onscreen text promoting the “largest tax cuts in history,” “reigniting American manufacturing” and a call to “defend law and order and police.”

The White House in a statement on Friday defended the use of what it described as “public service announcements” and dismissed criticism of them as “deeply dishonest.”

“The announcements are very clearly not campaign ads; President Trump is not on the ballot and there is no call to action,” the White House said. “Instead, the announcements are a reminder for Americans to love their country and know why it’s worth defending — at home, at the border, and abroad.”

Examples cited by the White House include George W. Bush’s administration airing a campaign about a Medicare law and the Biden administration running one about COVID-19 vaccinations.
entries.author: The Associated Press

entries.title: The Nats Close Out the Year With a 6-4 Win Over the Mets
entries.summary: Washington finishes the season with a 77-85 record, good for fourth place in the NL East.
entries.content:
Andrés Chaparro homered twice and the Washington Nationals defeated the New York Mets 6-4 on Sunday in the season finale for both teams.

Francisco Lindor hit his 300th career home run, Ronny Mauricio went deep for the third time in two days and rookie Carson Benge had three hits for his 45th multihit game and 14th with three or more for New York.

The Mets, who opened the season with a major league-record $358.4 million payroll, slid nine games from last year to 74-88 — their worst mark since going 70-92 in 2017. They finished last in the NL East for the first time since 2003.

New York was 34-47 under manager Carlos Mendoza, who was fired June 26, and 40-41 under Andy Green. The Mets lifted Green’s interim tag Tuesday and gave him a three-year contract through 2029.

The Nationals improved 11 games to 77-85 in manager Blake Butera’s first season. They finished fourth in the NL East while recording their seventh consecutive losing season since winning the 2019 World Series.

Chaparro led off the third and fifth innings with home runs against Mets starter Sean Manaea (6-8). It was Chaparro’s second career multihomer game and first since July 17.

After waiting out an hour-long rain delay at the start, New York built a 4-1 lead with the help of Mauricio and Lindor’s back-to-back home runs in the second. Lindor had not homered since Sept. 12.

Washington tied it with one run in the second and two in the third.

Will Dion (3-2) pitched two scoreless innings and Erik Tolman got four outs for his fifth save.

Manaea allowed five runs in six innings and struck out three.

Mets left fielder Juan Soto was 0 for 5 a day after exiting in the ninth inning when he got hit on his right hand by a pitch. Soto batted .275 with 27 homers and 68 RBIs in the second season of a $765 million, 15-year deal, and his .908 OPS was the second-lowest of his career.
entries.author: The Associated Press
